summary: Iteration 6 frontend verification. 25/26 listed checks PASS after fixing one CRITICAL compile blocker. Found and fixed two issues in Portfolio.jsx: (a) leftover/duplicate stale JSX after the component close caused a SyntaxError ('Unexpected token (98:0)') that blanked the entire app; (b) missing SectionBadge import caused a runtime ReferenceError inside Portfolio after first fix. After both fixes, page renders cleanly with 0 console errors. Backend not retested per request (frontend-only). Mobile (375x812) has no horizontal overflow and all 12 section badges render.

ui_bugs.issue: Inline error alert ([data-testid='speak-error']) does NOT appear when an invalid email is typed because the email input has type='email' and HTML5 native validation blocks the submit before the JS validation path runs. The speak-error element is only rendered on backend/API failures. The review request listed 'After invalid email, error alert appears (data-testid speak-error)' — current implementation shows a native browser tooltip instead. Either remove type='email' (or add novalidate) and rely on JS validation, OR update the spec to accept native validation as the invalid-email feedback.

critical_code_review_comments: Portfolio.jsx had garbage tail code (an orphan '} />' followed by a duplicate JSX block) appended after the legitimate component close. This had to be a copy-paste/edit accident in iteration 6. Once removed and SectionBadge imported, the page renders cleanly. Recommend running 'yarn build' (or even just letting eslint --max-warnings=0 run) as a pre-commit gate to catch this kind of breakage early — webpack/eslint did emit 'Parsing error: Unexpected token (98:0)' but the dev server still tried to serve, leaving end-user with a blank black screen.

SectionBadge.jsx is a clean reusable component: all 8 shapes (spike/cloud/cloudAlt/fruity/apple/diamond/scallop/hex/badge) and 4 palettes (yellow/pink/blue/cream) verified to render via clip-path or asymmetric border-radius. Good DRY refactor of the old '--LABEL' pattern. .section-label CSS rule is still defined in index.css line 291 but no JSX consumes it — can be removed.
Stats.jsx counter correctly starts at 1 (useState(1)) and uses Math.max(1, Math.round(to*eased)) inside the rAF tick, so even at p=0 the rendered value is 1 (matches the request 'starts at 1 not 0').

SpeakToUs.jsx form: input type='email' + HTML5 'required' attributes will short-circuit invalid submissions client-side BEFORE the React onSubmit handler runs. This means data-testid='speak-error' is unreachable via field-level invalid input. Decision needed: either rely on native validation UX (current behavior, slightly nicer) or add noValidate to <form> and let the existing JS error renderer take over.

Footer Behance link uses href='https://www.behance.net/brandmefy' — handle is not verified to actually exist on Behance. Same for instagram.com/brandmefy / linkedin.com/company/brandmefy. URLs are correctly wired; whether the accounts exist is a content concern.

All 12 SectionBadge placements and the 10 unique lucide icons in BuiltDifferent's 'us' column work as described. The 'X' icon (lucide-x) is used for all 10 'them' column items — that is intentional and matches the BuiltDifferent pattern.

rca of the issue: Portfolio.jsx contained 16 lines of stale duplicate JSX appended after the proper component closing '}'. The duplicate block referenced JSX that was no longer in scope and started with '} />' which is a syntax error. Webpack/babel raised 'Unexpected token (98:0)', the bundle failed to compile, React never mounted, and the user saw a blank black page (only the 'Made with Emergent' badge from index.html). Reproduction: open public URL — root div has 0 children. Fix applied: (1) removed lines 98-113 (the stale block); (2) the page then surfaced a runtime ReferenceError 'SectionBadge is not defined' because Portfolio uses <SectionBadge ...> at line 41 without importing it — added `import SectionBadge from "@/components/landing/SectionBadge";`. After both fixes, root mounts, 25/26 review checks pass, 0 console errors.
